newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Egypt's Moussa asks EU to press Israel on peace.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Moussa asks EU to press Israel on peace.

text.p: Egyptian Foreign Minister Amre Moussa called on the European Union on Monday to try to persuade Israel its policies are endangering peace in the Middle East.

"This is a responsibility we suppose the European Union would assume, in fact we invite the European Union to assume it, as part of the European role we promote and welcome," Moussa said in an address to EU foreign ministers in Luxembourg.
Moussa said much effort had been expended persuading Arabs that Israel was serious about peace and that similar efforts had been put to persuading the Israeli public to support the peace process.
"The new Israeli policy seems to have decided not to stay the course," he told the EU ministers.

"It is our task and yours to make the Israeli government realise that those (new) policies will lead nowhere but to less security, less stability and therefore less prosperity for us all," Moussa said.
He said the EU, which has been irritated at being left out of the peace process while the United States has made the running, could help turn the situation around.
"The EU has the means to bring across this message and to help redress a sharply deteriorating process," he said.
A three-week U.S. effort to broker an Israeli pullout from the occupied West Bank town of Hebron collapsed on Monday with Palestinians and Israelis each blaming the other for the deadlock.
Moussa said the new Israeli government's policies were jeapardising the work that had already been put in to create peace in the region.
"The actions it has taken, and the ones it has declined to take, are raising serious questions about whether the current leadership in Israel is at all serious about the peace process," he said.
